prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1070; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim received via first notice of loss call. Insured reports being rear-ended at a stop light by another vehicle. Insured states no airbag deployment and vehicle drivable from scene. Other driver's carrier identified. Reserve set for property damage and bodily injury pending review.

Entry 2: Contacted claimant's counsel's office to confirm representation and request all medical authorizations. Counsel advised that the claimant has been treating for neck and back strain and that all future communication should go through their office. Direct contact with claimant discontinued per counsel's request.

Entry 3: Received police report and photos of both vehicles. Rear bumper damage consistent with the reported impact. Estimate of repairs obtained from the body shop and reviewed. Supplement noted for hidden damage to the rear quarter panel. Liability assessed as clear in favor of claimant based on the report.

Entry 4: Received treatment records from claimant's counsel. Diagnosis includes cervical and lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Physical therapy recommended for several weeks. Demand package anticipated; requested itemized medical bills and wage loss documentation through counsel. Bodily injury reserve adjusted to reflect ongoing treatment.

Entry 5: Follow-up with claimant's counsel regarding status of records and demand timeline. Counsel indicated the demand will be submitted once treatment concludes. Reviewed reserve adequacy with supervisor. Diary set for next status check. No settlement authority requested at this time.
